title: The Export Relay
hookFX: Frame 0: black, then a giant split-flap board slams in and spins to 07. Sub-bass hit + camera shake on the 07. The baton (orange pill) is tossed across frame and freezes mid-air on DROP ONE?
concept: Export cargo is a relay baton passed through seven hands. One long shot, no cuts.
design: Isometric miniature diorama on cream paper. GPT-made 3D objects (warehouse, truck, customs booth, terminal crane, ship) sit along one long panorama. Handoff numbers on an airport-style split-flap board.
motion: Continuous horizontal camera dolly with soft ease-in-out at each station. Numbers change with a split-flap flip.
transition: No cuts. The camera slides to the next station.
beats: Seven handoffs. Drop one, and your cargo misses the ship.
One: booking. You lock space on a vessel. Every ship has a cut-off.
Two: the container is stuffed and weighed. Three: a truck runs it to the port.
Four: customs. The export declaration, the PEB, is filed before the container enters the port. Green lane: NPE issued. Red lane: inspection first.
04 PEB → NPE / GREEN: GO · RED: CHECK
Five: loaded, and the bill of lading is issued. Six: destination port. Seven: your buyer.
Miss one cut-off, and your container rolls to the next ship.
UGC Logistics carries the baton from stuffing to B/L. Ocean, air, and every export document, handled by one team.
Planning an export? Talk to UGC Logistics. We care what we deliver.
learn: The seven handoffs of an export shipment, and why cut-offs and the PEB-to-NPE step decide whether cargo makes the ship.
promo: One team holds the whole chain, so no handoff falls between two vendors.

music.prompt: Epic, upbeat and cheerful cinematic pop-orchestral track, 124 BPM, major key. Opens on a huge sub-bass boom and taiko hit, then marching snare and handclaps drive a steady build. Bright brass stabs on every handoff, soaring strings. Tension drop with a reverse cymbal at 0:33, then a euphoric full-band lift at 0:38. Clean button ending at 0:55. Instrumental, no vocals.
music.cues: 0:00 boom · 0:04 groove in · 0:33 drop out · 0:38 full lift · 0:53 button

facts: The PEB must be filed no earlier than 7 days before the expected export date and no later than when goods enter the customs area at the port of loading (bulk and a few other cases are exempt).
Export lanes in CEISA 4.0: green lane gets the NPE without physical inspection; red lane gets a physical inspection before the NPE is issued.
Since 1 July 2016 (SOLAS), a packed container needs a verified gross mass (VGM) before it is loaded. No VGM, no loading.
"Seven handoffs" is our simplified model of the chain, not a legal count. Say it as a story device, not a statistic.

title: Gate by Gate: Import Clearance
hookFX: Frame 0: a container drops from the top of frame and slams into a closed gate. Steel-impact boom, sodium lights flicker, dust burst. Text slams word by word.
concept: The container falls vertically through five gates and stops hard at each one before it may continue.

motion: Gravity: fast fall, hard stop with a springy bounce at each gate. The camera follows downward.
transition: A gate arm sweeps across the screen.
beats: The ship docked. Your cargo didn't move. Here's why.
Gate one: your container is unloaded and stacked in the port's temporary storage.
Gate two: import duties and taxes are paid, and the import declaration, the PIB, is filed with customs.
Gate three: the system assigns a lane. Green: released without a physical check. Red: goods and documents are inspected first.
Gate four: customs issues the SPPB, your release. Then the shipping line's delivery order.
Data doesn't match? Every extra day can add storage and container charges.
Gate five is UGC Logistics: documents checked, clearance handled, cargo trucked to your warehouse.
Importing soon? Let UGC Logistics open the gates. We care what we deliver.

promo: Customs & Import Solutions handles every gate, door to door.

facts: Only two import release lanes exist now: green and red. The yellow lane was removed by PER-02/BC/2022, effective 25 April 2022. The current guideline is PER-2/BC/2023 (effective 14 January 2023), implementing PMK 190/2022.
DDTC News: DJBC hapus jalur kuning
Green lane: no physical inspection; document review happens after the SPPB. Red lane: physical inspection and document review before the SPPB (the system issues an SPJM).
Do not say a document mismatch "sends you to the red lane". Lanes come from importer and commodity risk profiles, random selection and intelligence. A mismatch causes questions and delays.
No tariff or tax percentages in the video. Rates differ by HS code, origin and importer status.

title: Blueprint: Too Big for the Road
hookOS: TOO BIG FOR THE ROAD. MOVING ANYWAY.
hookFX: Frame 0: a giant transformer drops into frame and lands with a deep boom, camera shake and dust. Dimension lines snap out from its edges with a mechanical clack.

TOO BIG FOR THE ROAD. / MOVING ANYWAY.
Step one: survey the route. Bridges, tight corners, overhead cables. Every one gets measured.
Step two: permits. Oversized cargo needs approval from transport authorities, and often a police escort.
Step three: the right equipment. A lowbed or multi-axle trailer, plus a lifting plan for the crane.
Step four: lashing. The load is chained and secured, then moves slowly on a planned schedule.
UGC Logistics runs project and specialized cargo: oversized, heavy lift, industrial.
Got cargo that won't fit a normal truck? Talk to UGC Logistics.

title: Incoterms: Where Risk Switches
hookFX: Frame 0: a giant slider knob slams onto a route line with a click-boom; the line flashes red where risk switches. Warning-light pulse.
concept: One route line with a slider. The knob position is where cost and risk move from seller to buyer.
design: App-interface look: cards, toggles, small labels. Clean and tidy.
motion: The knob slides as if dragged by a finger, labels flip. A hand cursor appears.
transition: The screen scrolls to the next term.
beats: FOB on a container? Risky choice.
Incoterms 2020 decide where cost and risk switch sides.
EXW: the buyer takes over at the seller's door.
DDP: the seller delivers to the buyer's door, duties paid.
FOB and CIF: risk moves once goods are on board. CIF sellers still pay the freight.
For containers, FCA or CIP usually fit better.
Whatever term you sign, UGC Logistics handles your part.
UGC Logistics. We care what we deliver.
learn: Where cost and risk transfer under EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and why FCA or CIP suit containers.
promo: UGC handles the shipper's or buyer's share under any Incoterm.

facts: Incoterms 2020 is the edition in force. ICC has begun groundwork for a 2030 revision but has published no new text or date.

Under FOB and CIF, risk passes when goods are on board the vessel at the port of shipment. CIF sellers pay freight and minimum insurance (ICC Clauses C) to the destination port; CIP requires Clauses A.
For containerized cargo handed over at a terminal, FCA, CPT or CIP generally fit better than FOB or CIF.
Incoterms® is a registered ICC trademark. Write it as "Incoterms® 2020" in on-screen text.

title: The Weight You Can't See
hookFX: Frame 0: a scale needle slams from 50 to 80 with a heavy mechanical clunk and a boom. Warning lamps flash.

music.prompt: Fast, cheerful and epic retro-future track, 130 BPM, major key. Heavy mechanical clunk and boom at the start, then driving drums, bright analog synth lead and short brass hits on each needle swing. Lift at 0:18. Final hit at 0:24. Instrumental, no vocals.

facts: Air chargeable weight = the higher of actual weight and volumetric weight. Standard IATA divisor: L × W × H (cm) ÷ 6,000. Express couriers often use 5,000. Example in the hook: a 100 × 100 × 48 cm box = 80 kg volumetric; if it weighs 50 kg, you pay for 80 kg.
Show the box dimensions on screen (100 × 100 × 48 cm) so the 80 kg figure is checkable. No transit times or prices.

title: HS 2028: The Codes Are Changing
hookFX: Frame 0: thousands of digits rain down and slam into one line with a glitch boom: 2028. The screen cracks into a grid of code cells.

beats: In 2028, the world's product codes change.
HS codes classify every traded product. The first six digits are shared worldwide.
Indonesia adds two more from the ASEAN tariff list: eight digits in total.
That code sets your import duty and the rules your goods must follow.
HS 2028 brings hundreds of changes. Some codes will need a second look.
UGC Logistics checks your codes before customs does.
